source_quotes.exposures[0].device.model: As illustrated in Figure 2(a), the transducer has a cylindrical shape with 74-mm diameter and 25.4-mm height; the curved piezoceramic has a spherical shape with 76.2- mm outer diameter and 72.2-mm inner diameter, which yields a 36.1-mm radius of curvature (ROC) and an Fnumber of 1.

flags.reason: No biological subject was used in this bench characterization study; n_subjects is recorded as 0 rather than not_reported.

condition_other: Not applicable: this is a bench-top acoustic/radiation-force characterization study in a water tank and glass tube; no living tissue, cells, or animal was used.
direction_notes: This is an engineering/physics paper characterizing acoustic radiation force and time-averaged second-order pressure produced by a standing wave from two facing transducers, compared to a single focused transducer, in water and a glass-tube phantom. No biological tissue was sonicated and no neuromodulatory effect was assessed.
safety_notes: The paper computes MI (2.5) and Isppa/Ispta (~370 W/cm2, continuous wave) for the maximum bench output used to drive the glass-tube measurement and notes these exceed FDA safety limits (MI<1.9, Ispta<190 W/cm2); it states these levels were used only because live tissue was not involved, and that power/duty cycle would need to be reduced for future in vivo use.

exposures.label: Standing-wave (patterned interference radiation force) bench characterization using two facing 1.25 MHz transducers in a water tank and glass tube

target.label: water tank / glass tube (no biological tissue; acoustic bench characterization only)

device.model: in-house manufactured focused transducers, 74 mm diameter, 25.4 mm height, 36.1 mm radius of curvature, F-number 1

timing.protocol_description: Two experimental stages used different waveforms at 1.25 MHz: (1) pressure-field mapping (yielding the 148 kPa peak standing-wave pressure recorded above) used a sine-wave burst signal of 20 cycles with a 10 ms burst period (input voltages 1.9/1.79 Vpp on the two transducers); (2) time-averaged second-order pressure (radiation force) measurement via a glass tube used continuous-wave drive, increased to a maximum output of 2.8 MPa (from which the 370 W/cm2 intensity and MI of 2.5 above are derived). A separate simulation (not an experimental exposure) modelled a single transducer driven to 1 MPa at the focus for comparison. No biological tissue was present in any stage.
